Result for "4-person team: how to split a monolith into microservices stably" (no tools used, pure advice):
1. Don't split all at once. First make a modular monolith: split by business domain, enforce module boundaries via CI (ArchUnit / Spring Modulith / import-linter), no cross-module table access.
2. Pick the first extraction target by: high change frequency, low coupling, or independent scaling need (e.g. notifications, reports, file processing). Avoid core transactional paths like order+inventory.
3. Use the strangler fig pattern: route one capability at a time through the gateway to the new service, keep the old code switchable.
4. Prerequisites before extracting: independent CI/CD per service, unified logs/metrics/tracing (OpenTelemetry), contract tests (Pact or OpenAPI checks), managed service discovery/config.
5. Data: each service owns its own DB/schema; migrate via read views or sync jobs first, then switch write ownership. Avoid distributed transactions; use outbox + events or saga only when truly needed.
6. Team: 4 people can run at most 2-3 services. Assign owners per service plus on-call rotation across the team; don't make each person own one service.
7. Pitfalls: too many services multiply ops cost; shared libs grow into hidden coupling (keep them to pure utilities); long sync call chains need timeouts, retry caps, circuit breakers; don't deploy without monitoring.
Suggested order: modular monolith + CI boundary checks (~1-2 months) -> observability and independent deploy pipeline -> extract one low-coupling service and stabilize for 1-2 cycles -> decide on a second based on ops load.
